All 4 candidates are direct/near-direct matches for the target trait (alcohol dependence) via trait_efo alignment (PGS002738/PGS002739: "alcohol dependence"; PGS000201/PGS000202: "alcohol dependence measurement") and phenotype alignment (all report alcohol use disorder endpoints, including DSM-5 criteria count for PGS000201/PGS000202). All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping_reported aligns via Angina/I20 ICD10/PheCode 411.3). The strongest visible PRS-quality evidence comes from the HGG Adv MVP PheCode 411.3 set (PGS005048–PGS005059), which report per-SD effect sizes with CIs and C-index values; among them, PGS005048 has the highest reported C-index (0.7669) and a moderate-to-strong OR per SD (1.487, 95% CI 1.41–1.56), making it the best-supported single pick from the available metadata. Runners-up are selected from the same MVP family based on near-identical endpoint/covariates and slightly lower but very similar C-index and OR evidence (PGS005052: C-index 0.7662, OR 1.491; PGS005057: 0.7664, OR 1.479; PGS005051: 0.7655, OR 1.455; PGS005058: 0.7656, OR 1.452). Confidence is not High because several MVP candidates are effectively near-ties on the key comparable signals, and other direct-match options either lack PRS-comparable metrics (e.g., PGS004457/PGS004527 only OR without discrimination metrics) or come from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262) where full-model AUROC is likely covariate-driven and framework origin is a known generalization risk; additionally, some candidates report only full-model metrics or have missing/unknown covariate detail, limiting decisive separation.

Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254) plus closely related aortic valve function measures mapped to aortic stenosis (PGS005255/PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported because it is an exact trait match (trait_reported/trait_efo = aortic stenosis) with endpoint-fidelity consistent with the target (phenotyping_reported: incident aortic stenosis cases), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) with large variant count (~1.12M), and reports a strong time-to-event discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) alongside a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.92). Main limitation: the reported discrimination is a full-model metric with multiple clinical covariates (e.g., T2D, HTN, CAD, hyperlipidemia, BMI, smoking, renal failure), and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the PRS-only contribution cannot be isolated from covariate-driven performance. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS005254 is also an exact aortic stenosis model with incident endpoint and HR 1.64 but lacks comparable discrimination metrics; PGS005255 and PGS005256 are aortic stenosis–mapped valve-function traits with the same incident AS phenotyping and moderate HR (~1.53) but are less directly aligned by trait_reported; among the remaining non-AS models, PGS000739 is included last as the closest available (cardiomyopathy) but is not a direct phenotype match to aortic stenosis.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including PGS001135 ("Arthritis (nos)") and two "Other arthritis" models (PGS004477, PGS004547). PGS001135 is the best-supported direct match on endpoint fidelity because its trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are explicitly "arthritis" / "Arthritis (nos)", whereas many other listed models are specific arthritis subtypes (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, osteoarthritis, gout) rather than the generic umbrella target. However, the evidence is sub-optimal because PGS001135 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits"), and its PRS-only metrics are weak (PGS-only AUROC 0.539 and PGS R2 0.00291; incremental AUROC 0.00314), suggesting limited standalone PRS signal for generic arthritis. The runners-up are the other explicit arthritis EFO models (PGS004477, PGS004547), but they provide only modest effect-size evidence (OR ~1.20–1.26) and lack comparable PRS-only discrimination metrics; remaining alternatives (e.g., osteoarthritis knee/hip) are arthritis-adjacent but not exact arthritis endpoints.

All listed candidates are direct matches to asthma (trait_efo=asthma), but they vary in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable evidence. PGS002727 is preferred because it is explicitly a disease-focused pediatric asthma PRS (phenotyping_reported: Pediatric asthma) with strong PRS-discrimination evidence via effect size (OR per SD 1.57, 95% CI 1.55–1.60) and a reported full-model AUROC of 0.66; it is also evaluated across multiple ancestries (EVAL includes AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/SAS), supporting transportability. However, covariates are listed as Unknown and the endpoint is pediatric-specific rather than generic asthma, which lowers certainty for a broad 'asthma' target and prevents a high-quality designation.

Runners-up: PGS001782 (PRS-CS-auto; asthma; AUROC 0.659 and covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2 0.048844 in EUR) has strong PRS-comparable R2 evidence but appears to come from a global biobank framework-style paper; PGS001787 is similar but with weaker R2 (0.035168) and AUROC (0.64). PGS001344 (UKB snpnet; doctor-diagnosed asthma) has strong endpoint fidelity and the best full-model AUROC among the snpnet siblings (0.66621) with reported PGS-only AUROC/R2, but it is from a pan-trait '813 traits' framework which is penalized versus disease-focused models. PGS002061 (LDpred2; UKB portability study) has supportive partial-r (0.1184) but lacks clearer PRS-only AUROC/R2 and is also a framework/portability context, making it less compelling than the above. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct EFO matches to atopic eczema, but endpoint fidelity differs. PGS002755 is the best-supported direct match because its phenotyping_reported is "Incident atopic dermatitis" (generic disease endpoint aligned to target) and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants), with a reported HR (high vs low PRS)=1.249 (EUR eval; n=337,910). Main limitation: no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is reported, and the HR is modest.

Runners-up: PGS004587 is also incident atopic dermatitis with a similar HR=1.153 (n=337,910) but is a sparse 23-variant GWAS-hits score and comes from an air-pollution integration context, making it structurally weaker for standalone PRS. PGS001773 targets "Moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis" (subtype mismatch vs generic eczema) and reports a very high full-model AUROC=0.93 and R²=0.49, but these are full-model metrics with multiple demographic/ethnicity covariates and are not PRS-comparable; the magnitude also strains plausibility relative to the provided heritability ceiling guidance, lowering trust in the PRS contribution. PGS003459 and PGS003486 are atopic-eczema-related but their phenotyping is "Paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis" (therapy/setting-specific endpoint), so despite reporting AUROC ~0.58 and ORs, they are less faithful to generic atopic eczema risk.

All listed candidates are direct matches to atrial fibrillation (or AF/flutter) by trait_reported/trait_efo and generally endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported. PGS005168 is best supported because it comes from a disease-focused large AF meta-analysis publication (Nat Genet; >180k cases per title), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), reports a strong effect size (HR=1.6663) and a high discrimination metric (C-index=0.8718 with CI), and has extensive performance record support (record_count=45) with European validation specified. Key limitation: the reported C-index appears to be a full-model metric (covariates include CHARGE-AF), so the very high C-index may be substantially covariate-driven and is not directly comparable to PRS-only performance; this lowers confidence from High to Moderate.

Runners-up: PGS005313 is also disease-focused multi-cohort (Nat Commun) with strong OR=1.82 and AUROC=0.78 and basic covariates (age, sex), but has only one performance record visible here. PGS002814 has very large GWAS training (n=1,150,799) and strong OR (~1.94) with AUROC=0.74, but is explicitly developed/validated in East Asian context (MAE/EAS), making it less universally supported than the EUR-validated top pick in this context. PGS000016 (LDpred; 6.7M variants) has explicit PRS-only R2=0.029 (sanity-consistent with AF h2_obs~0.0204) and large validation (n=288,978), but is older and its strongest AUROC shown (0.77) is full-model. PGS000331 is disease-focused (Nat Med) with HR=1.62 and C-index=0.751, but has smaller training (n=21,813) and fewer supporting records than the top pick. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct matches via trait_efo including atrial flutter. PGS001263 is the only exact-label atrial flutter model and also reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.61716; PGS-only R2=0.02517) with basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), making its performance evidence more directly interpretable than models lacking PRS-only AUC/R2. Its PRS-only R2 is below the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443), so there is no obvious sanity-check violation. Main limitation: it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework (snpnet; ‘across 813 traits’), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly, and its full-model AUROC (~0.78) is likely largely covariate-driven given small incremental AUROC (~0.022). Runner-up PGS001339 is also from the same framework but has a time-to-event combined AF+flutter endpoint (less endpoint-fidelitous to pure flutter) and slightly weaker PRS-only metrics. PGS002050 and PGS001841 (UKB portability paper) have combined AF+flutter endpoints and broader multi-ancestry evaluation, but they lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 (only partial-r ~0.103), reducing comparability and making them harder to rank above the exact flutter model despite potentially stronger method structure (LDpred2) for polygenic traits.

Two direct-match candidates are present for autism spectrum disorder (ASD): PGS000327 and PGS002790. PGS000327 is best supported because its phenotype alignment is coherent across fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all explicitly ASD), it comes from an ASD-focused publication (“Identification of common genetic risk variants for autism spectrum disorder.”), and it provides supportive PRS signal evidence including an OR per SD of 1.33 (moderate) and a reported full_model_r2 of 0.0245 in European validation with basic covariates (genetic PCs, genotyping wave). PGS002790 is a weaker direct match despite the ASD label because phenotyping_reported is explicitly different (“Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)”), suggesting endpoint-fidelity mismatch; its reported partial R² (0.00546) is also smaller and it lacks effect-size reporting. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because neither model reports clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (AUC/PRS-only R² are null), and the best model’s performance evidence is limited to a full-model R²/effect size without clearer PRS-only metrics.

The strongest-supported choice is PGS000452 because it has high endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported = Basal cell carcinoma), basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs), and the strongest visible performance package among the MGI Cancer PRSweb siblings: full-model AUROC 0.632 (0.616–0.647) with the largest reported per-SD effect size (OR 1.663, 1.57–1.761) and strong top-1% vs rest OR (3.61). Runners-up are other endpoint-faithful, basic-covariate models with very similar AUROC and effect sizes: PGS000454 (AUROC 0.632; OR 1.661; top-1% OR 3.79), PGS000456 (AUROC 0.63; OR 1.633; top-1% OR 3.95), and PGS000458 (AUROC 0.628; OR 1.634; top-1% OR 4.03). All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait via trait_efo including “bilirubin metabolism disease.” The strongest endpoint-fidelity matches are PGS001824 and PGS002032 (phenotyping_reported/trait_reported: “Disorders of bilirubin excretion”), whereas PGS000924 uses a broader composite time-to-event endpoint (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism (time-to-event)”), which domain guidance flags as a weaker endpoint form when cleaner direct disease endpoints exist. Between the two exact-endpoint siblings (PGS001824 vs PGS002032), the visible performance evidence is essentially identical (same partial-r 0.0716 with overlapping CIs; no PRS-only AUROC/R² reported), so method/structure becomes the main differentiator: LDpred2 (PGS002032) is a genome-wide shrinkage approach with far more variants (19,768) than the penalized regression score (PGS001824; 22 variants), which is a supportive structural signal for polygenic capture given no contrary metric evidence. Confidence is limited because the key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) are missing for both top candidates, and the only available metric (partial-r) is modest and does not separate them; additionally, PGS000924 reports unusually high R²/AUROC relative to the provided heritability ceiling and comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper, making its performance less reliable for selection despite having explicit AUC/R² fields.

Direct-match candidates are present (3 total) and all come from the same publication, method family (SDPR), training cohort (PGC), and EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, with similarly tiny reported partial R² values (~0.0025–0.0031) and no PRS-only AUROC/AUC. However, endpoint fidelity is unclear/possibly mismatched across all three because phenotyping_reported fields are non-diagnostic behavioral/cognitive measures rather than bipolar disorder case-control status, making it hard to justify any as a clearly strong bipolar-disorder PRS. Given the target is broad “bipolar disorder,” PGS002786 is selected as best only because its trait_reported/trait_efo most directly match the target label (bipolar disorder vs bipolar I/II subtypes), while runners-up are the subtype scores (PGS002787, PGS002788). Confidence is low because the primary endpoint/phenotyping mismatch and lack of PRS-comparable performance metrics prevent a high-quality direct-match recommendation.

Direct-match candidates are present (3 total) but none is a clearly strong, endpoint-faithful match for the broad target label "blood coagulation disease" based on the visible phenotype fields, and two candidates map to a narrower congenital deficiency EFO rather than the target EFO.

Best pick: PGS001033 is the only candidate whose trait_efo exactly matches the target (blood coagulation disease) and it reports PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.634) and PGS-only R² (0.0578), with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). However, its phenotyping_reported is explicitly time-to-event ("TTE other coagulation defects"), and it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as a systematic generalization weakness; additionally, the score is extremely sparse (variants_number=1), further limiting confidence.

Runners-up: PGS002034 and PGS001826 both target "Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)" with trait_efo "congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency" (narrower than the target), and neither reports AUROC/R²; they only report partial correlation (~0.056). Between them, PGS002034 is structurally preferred due to a much larger variant count (32,552; LDpred2) versus PGS001826 (45; penalized regression), while other visible fields (publication family, cohorts, covariates, validation size, ancestry) are essentially identical.

Direct-match candidates are abundant for breast carcinoma. The strongest-supported option in the visible list is PGS004153 because it is directly aligned to breast cancer (trait_efo=breast carcinoma; phenotyping_reported=Breast cancer), uses a multi-score aggregation approach (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV; a positive structural signal per domain_knowledge), and has the highest reported full-model AUROC among the tightly clustered 2023-12-19 UKB method-benchmark family (AUROC=0.6625 with R²=0.0764; covariates reported as 0, reducing concern about covariate-driven inflation relative to models using clinical calculators/family history). Runners-up are selected from the same coherent high-support family with the next-best, very similar AUROC/R² evidence and the same endpoint/covariate structure: PGS004040 (LDpred2.CV; AUROC=0.6598, R²=0.0739), PGS004025 (LDpred2-auto; AUROC=0.6598, R²=0.0736), PGS004083 (PRS-CS-auto; AUROC=0.6553, R²=0.0697), and PGS004069 (megaprs.CV; AUROC=0.6558, R²=0.0709). Confidence is Moderate (not High) because the evidence relies on full-model AUROC/R² from one benchmarking publication family (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² fields shown here), and several near-tied candidates within that family are effectively very close in reported performance, making the exact ordering somewhat sensitive to small metric differences.

All 10 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo=celiac disease), with generally good endpoint fidelity (most have phenotyping_reported as coeliac/celiac disease; two are restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers; two are broader composites including gluten sensitivity). PGS000316 is best supported overall because it is a disease-focused celiac-disease score (phenotyping_reported: Coeliac disease) with strong reported discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.879 with CI) and very large validation sample size (n=379,767), making it the most empirically supported direct-match in the provided list. Key limitation: covariates are listed as Unknown for PGS000316 (and several others), so the AUROC is not clearly PRS-only and comparability across models is imperfect; this keeps confidence below High. Runners-up were ranked by remaining direct-match support combining endpoint fidelity and availability/strength of PRS-comparable metrics: PGS001301 reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC=0.8287; PGS R2=0.1422; full-model AUROC=0.8335) but comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a known weaker archetype per domain knowledge) and uses a broader phenotype label (malabsorption/coeliac disease). PGS000040 is disease-focused with very high reported AUROC (0.90) but only as a full-model metric with unknown covariates and smaller validation (n=2,476). PGS000042 and PGS000041 are disease-focused but restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers (endpoint narrower than generic celiac disease), with moderate full-model AUROC (~0.73 and ~0.718). Other direct matches (PGS001856/PGS002067 and the gluten-sensitivity composites PGS001894/PGS002107) have weaker or less directly comparable performance reporting (partial-r only) and/or less specific endpoints, so they were not placed in the top 4 alternatives. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported are cervical cancer, mostly incident cervical cancer). PGS003428 is best supported overall because it comes from a cervical-phenotype-focused GWAS meta-analysis study (publication explicitly about cervical phenotypes and risk stratification), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred; 2,894,555 variants) consistent with stronger structural properties than sparse/GWAS-hit scores, and reports a moderate per-SD effect size (HR=1.33) with basic covariates (age, smoking) and EUR evaluation. Main limitation: it lacks PRS-only performance metrics (only full-model C-index=0.613 is shown), so the empirical performance comparability vs other direct-match models is uncertain, lowering confidence.

Runners-up: PGS000073 and PGS000784 have strong endpoint fidelity (incident cervical cancer) and large EUR validation (n=211,795) with similar reported full-model discrimination (~0.745 AUROC/C-index) and HR~1.21–1.22, but they are small GWAS-hit-style scores (10 variants) and their reported AUROC appears to be full-model (covariates include multiple epidemiologic factors), which domain guidance says should not be over-weighted as PRS quality evidence. PGS005165 is a direct-match EAS-only model (15 variants; C-index=0.566; HR=1.20) and is supported for East Asian contexts but has weaker reported discrimination and limited transportability evidence beyond EAS. PGS003389 is direct-match but shows weak discrimination (AUROC=0.563; R²=0.00158) despite many variants (lassosum; 2,814), making it less supported than the above. PGS001299 is deprioritized because it is from a pan-trait UKB framework ("813 traits" snpnet) with low PRS-only performance (PGS-only AUROC~0.55; PGS R²~0.0026), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused alternatives.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis via trait_efo/trait_reported, with two especially endpoint-faithful ICD10 K80 models (PGS004546, PGS004476). PGS004546 is best supported because it targets K80 (Cholelithiasis) with EUR development/evaluation and reports the strongest available per-SD effect size among the K80 siblings (OR=1.2986 vs 1.2194 for PGS004476), which is the most comparable PRS-quality signal available for that publication family given missing AUC/R2. Runners-up: PGS004476 is the closest sibling (same endpoint/method family/variants, slightly weaker OR). PGS001174 is a direct cholelithiasis model with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.623, PGS R2 0.028) and incremental AUROC reported, but it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework and uses a time-to-event phenotype, both of which are negative signals for external generalization despite good metric availability; its PRS-only R2 remains below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0214; liability h2=0.1372), so metrics are at least plausible. PGS002072 and PGS001861 are direct but use a broader composite endpoint (cholelithiasis and cholecystitis) and come from a UKB portability framework; they report only partial-r (0.098 and 0.0948), limiting comparability versus OR/AUC/R2. Overall confidence is moderate (not high) because most candidates lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2, covariates are unknown for the top K80 models, and the remaining candidates are framework-derived with limited comparable performance reporting.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = chronic kidney disease), so ranking is driven by endpoint fidelity plus the most PRS-informative performance evidence available (effect sizes / PRS-only metrics), while discounting covariate-inflated full-model AUROC. PGS002237 is best supported because it is explicitly CKD stage 3+ (eGFR<45) with a large development sample (n=279,819), multi-ancestry evaluation, and a relatively strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.47, 95% CI 1.32–1.65) from a CKD-focused Nat Med study; its reported AUROC (0.78) is full-model with many clinical covariates, so it is not treated as PRS-only, but the endpoint and effect size still provide strong direct-match support. Runners-up: PGS005090 shows very strong reported discrimination (AUROC=0.9; R2=0.1) and good endpoint alignment (CKD stage 3+), but it is AFR-only GWAS/EVAL and the very high metrics are not clearly PRS-only, making general direct-match strength less certain without deployment ancestry context. PGS005113 has a solid OR (1.35) and CKDGen training cohort with broad evaluation ancestries, but lacks PRS-only metrics and is from a proteomic-marker context rather than a CKD-prediction-focused paper. PGS004889 is incident CKD (without diabetes) with HR=1.3 and multi-ancestry evaluation, but the endpoint is restricted (incident, non-diabetic) and includes a bundled clinical risk score covariate, reducing PRS comparability. PGS002757 is a clean CKD label with modest OR=1.15 and EUR evaluation, but weaker effect size support than the higher-OR/HR alternatives. Confidence is Moderate because many candidates lack PRS-only AUROC/R2, several reported AUROCs are full-model and covariate-dependent, and multiple near-clone CKD models exist with limited directly comparable PRS-only metrics.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo = chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). PGS001783 is best supported overall because it is an exact COPD endpoint (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both COPD) and, among the visible direct matches, it provides comparatively strong PRS-comparable evidence via a covariates-regressed-out/Nagelkerke R2=0.038092 plus a reported AUROC=0.74 (noting the AUROC may reflect a full model per domain guidance), and it is built from a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant count (884,139) and multi-biobank development cohorts, which domain guidance treats as structurally favorable versus sparse/pan-trait UKB framework scores. The main limitation is that the reported AUROCs appear to be full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), so discrimination is not strictly comparable as standalone PRS evidence; this keeps confidence at Moderate. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS000325 and PGS000326 are JIA subtypes (oligoarticular; RF-negative polyarticular) with good endpoint fidelity but narrower than the target; PGS000324 is also a subtype (enthesitis-related) and despite very high full-model AUROC (0.93), subtype mismatch and reliance on full-model AUROC prevent it from outranking the broad JIA model. Only 3 distinct runners-up exist, so the last is repeated to maintain the required list length.

All 10 listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (kidney cancer) via trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (kidney cancer / renal carcinoma / renal cell carcinoma; several explicitly use incident kidney cancer endpoints). PGS004908 is best supported because it has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Kidney cancer), reports the strongest visible discrimination among candidates (AUROC 0.74 with CI 0.72–0.75) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.5, CI 1.43–1.58), with covariates that are standard epidemiologic adjustments (age, sex, PCs, BMI, smoking, hypertension) rather than obvious clinical-risk packaging. Main limitation: the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2), so comparability across studies is imperfect and confidence is reduced.

Runners-up ranking: PGS000076 and PGS000787 are highly endpoint-faithful (incident kidney cancer; renal cell carcinoma as dominant subtype) and show similar full-model AUROC (~0.722) plus HR ~1.15–1.16, but they are older cross-/pan-cancer evaluation contexts and still lack PGS-only metrics; PGS000722 has weaker AUROC (0.567) but strong endpoint fidelity and large evaluation; PGS004690 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (AnnoPred; 6.35M variants) which is structurally favorable, but its reported AUROC is modest (0.5644) and covariates are unknown, limiting support relative to the higher-performing direct candidates.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (kidney failure) are present, including PGS004562 and PGS004492 (both trait_efo: kidney failure; phenotyping_reported: N18 chronic renal failure) and PGS000708 (trait_reported: Kidney failure; but phenotyping_reported indicates diabetic kidney failure). PGS004562 is best supported on endpoint fidelity (explicit chronic renal failure/kidney failure code N18) and shows the strongest available per-SD effect size among the kidney-failure-labeled options (OR=1.39548 vs OR=1.1708 for PGS004492), with a genome-wide shrinkage method (RFDiseasemetaPRS). However, the evidence remains limited because these N18 models provide no PRS-comparable AUROC/R² and list covariates as Unknown, reducing comparability and interpretability. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS004492 (same endpoint but weaker OR), PGS000708 (kidney failure label but restricted to diabetic kidney failure and full-model C-index likely covariate-influenced), then near-synonymous CKD/chronic renal failure endpoints (PGS001272 time-to-event chronic renal failure from a pan-trait framework; PGS002237 CKD stage 3+ from a disease-focused Nat Med study but not kidney-failure-specific).

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target (trait_efo maps to knee osteoarthritis / gonarthrosis). PGS002767 is best supported because it has strong PRS-discrimination evidence via an OR per SD of 1.35 (with CI 1.3–1.4) on a directly aligned knee osteoarthritis endpoint, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with ~1.05M variants, and is evaluated in EUR (n=39,444) with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/technical), making the reported effect size more PRS-comparable than full-model AUROC-only reports. Runners-up: PGS002729 is also endpoint-aligned and disease-focused, but its only visible metric is a full-model AUROC (0.66) with BMI included and no PGS-only metrics/effect size, so PRS-specific performance is less clear. PGS004549 and PGS004479 are endpoint-aligned and use genome-wide methods with moderate ORs (~1.37 and ~1.32), but covariates are unknown and they come from a risk-factor integration framing, reducing comparability. PGS001192 reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.5566; PGS R2 0.0068) but is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (snpnet; 813 traits paper) and shows weak PRS-only signal, so it is not preferred over disease-focused alternatives. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because most candidates lack PRS-only AUC/R2 and several rely on full-model metrics or have unknown covariates, leaving residual uncertainty despite clear direct-match availability.

All 5 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo to late-onset Alzheimer’s disease, so a direct-match exists. PGS000054 is preferred because it is endpoint-faithful (familial late-onset AD/LOAD), uses only basic covariates (age, sex), and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.73, 95% CI 1.57–1.93), which domain guidance treats as strong discrimination evidence when PRS-only AUC/R2 are absent. Main limitation: none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R², so ranking relies heavily on effect sizes and endpoint coherence rather than directly comparable PRS metrics; additionally PGS000054’s evaluation ancestry is AMR-only, which may reduce generalizability if EUR deployment is intended. Runners-up: PGS000053 is the closest sibling (same study/endpoint/covariates) but with weaker OR (1.29). PGS000334 has a direct LOAD endpoint and reports an R²=0.191, but it appears to be a full-model/other-metric with unknown covariates and is unusually high for C+T, making comparability/sanity uncertain per the provided guidance. PGS004918 is endpoint-aligned but has very small development/validation (n=439 training; n=136 validation) and only a full-model AUROC (0.731) with unknown covariates, so PRS contribution is unclear. PGS002289 is labeled LOAD but its phenotyping_reported is a cognition-by-age interaction outcome rather than AD diagnosis, creating endpoint-fidelity concerns despite very large validation size.

Direct-match candidates for lung cancer are present (multiple models with trait_reported/phenotyping_reported explicitly lung cancer or closely synonymous endpoints like lung and bronchus cancer). PGS000078 is best supported overall because it has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: incident lung cancer), large European evaluation (n=392,539; EUR-only GWAS/EVAL), and includes effect-size evidence (HR=1.16, 95% CI 1.11–1.22) alongside reported discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.846; C-index 0.849). However, this is not DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY because the key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2 or incremental AUROC) are not provided, and the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics with extensive covariates (including family history, PM2.5, and detailed smoking terms), which domain guidance indicates can inflate/obscure the standalone PRS contribution. Runners-up were ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS000789 is essentially the same lung-cancer PRS (109 variants) with similar endpoint and metrics; PGS004860 reports very high full-model AUROC (0.893) but also lacks PRS-only metrics and uses covariates including smoking status; PGS000740 is lung-cancer-focused but is restricted to early-onset lung cancer (<50 years), making it less aligned to generic lung cancer; PGS000721 is a simpler genome-wide-significant-variants score with direct lung cancer endpoint but smaller validation (n=1,202) and less supporting performance detail.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (lupus erythematosus) via either the exact EFO term (lupus erythematosus) or the closely aligned clinical entity systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The best-supported choice is PGS000754 because its endpoint is a direct SLE diagnosis (phenotyping_reported: systemic lupus erythematosus) and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (lassosum) with very large variant coverage (293,684), which is structurally favored for polygenic traits over sparse GWAS-hit scores when PRS-only metrics are not available. Its reported AUROC (0.65) is only a full-model metric and therefore not directly comparable as PRS-only performance, but it is at least provided without explicit heavy clinical covariate packaging.

Runners-up: PGS000328 and PGS000196 are also direct SLE diagnosis-oriented models with higher reported full-model AUROC (0.83 and 0.79 respectively), but both are sparse (57 and 55 variants) and have phenotype restrictions/contexts that reduce generality (early-onset SLE for PGS000328; SLE diagnosis in an inflammatory arthritis outpatient context for PGS000196). PGS004917 is a direct SLE model with moderate full-model AUROC (0.696) and strong reported effect sizes (OR 2.01), but it is explicitly an interaction-focused study (genetics × smoking), which raises comparability concerns for a standalone PRS. PGS001870 is an exact-label lupus erythematosus model, but it comes from a UK Biobank portability framework and reports only a small partial correlation (0.0184), making it weaker than disease-focused SLE models despite the label match.

Main limitation driving DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL: across the pool, PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2 or incremental metrics) are largely absent, and several candidates have endpoint restrictions or covariate/packaging concerns (e.g., phenotype risk score covariate in PGS003960; nephritis/renal-onset subphenotypes in PGS003755/PGS003756/PGS000771/PGS000772), preventing a clearly high-confidence single winner based solely on the visible evidence.

Direct-match candidates are present for lymphoid leukemia (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305) and closely aligned chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) candidates (PGS000646/647/648/649/650/651, PGS000874, PGS003453). PGS000788 is best supported within the visible list because it has a directly aligned endpoint (phenotyping_reported: incident lymphocytic leukemia; trait_efo: lymphoid leukemia), uses the same 75-variant set as PGS000077, and shows the strongest reported per-SD effect size among the direct lymphoid/lymphocytic leukemia models (HR=1.7) with strong full-model discrimination (AUROC=0.738; C-index=0.756) under basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs). Main limitation: the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2), so PRS-only performance is uncertain; additionally, several high-performing CLL-specific scores exist but are subtype-specific relative to the broader target. Runners-up: PGS000077 is the closest sibling with the same endpoint and similar covariates but weaker reported HR (1.45) and AUROC (0.719). PGS000874 has very strong discrimination (C-index=0.861) and OR=3.79 but is explicitly in a family-history-enriched subgroup, reducing generalizability to generic lymphoid leukemia risk. Among the clean CLL PRSweb siblings, PGS000648 and PGS000646 have the strongest reported AUROC (~0.696) and OR (~2.12/2.10) with consistent EUR evaluation, but remain subtype-specific (chronic lymphocytic leukemia) rather than the broader lymphoid leukemia target.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (macular degeneration / age-related macular degeneration), but they vary in endpoint fidelity and in whether reported metrics are PRS-comparable. PGS004606 is best supported overall because it has clean phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: "Age-related macular degeneration"), comes from a disease-focused AMD GWAS study family (Nat Genet 2024), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.0M variants), and reports a validation AUROC (0.71) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), making the evidence package coherent. Runners-up: PGS004952 reports a much higher AUROC but it is a full-model metric (no PGS-only metric shown) on a narrower endpoint (late AMD) with a small validation sample (n=1,232) and an apparent AUROC formatting inconsistency (84.2 vs 0.842), so it is supportive but less reliable; PGS004607 is a sibling from the same Nat Genet study family but shows weaker AUROC (0.65) in EUR evaluation and is based on AFR GWAS; PGS001013 is an exact-label macular degeneration model but is from a pan-trait UKB sparse framework ("across 813 traits") with weak PGS-only AUROC (~0.553) and small incremental AUROC, suggesting limited PRS signal; among the UKB portability models, PGS002041 slightly edges PGS001834 and PGS002269 on structural grounds (LDpred2 genome-wide vs penalized regression with far fewer variants, and PGS002269’s phenotyping_reported is a retinal thickness biomarker rather than direct AMD diagnosis), but all three are limited by lacking PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (only small partial-r for the portability scores). Main limitation: across the strongest disease-focused candidates, the available performance evidence is mostly full-model AUROC rather than explicit PGS-only metrics, reducing certainty in ranking strength.

Direct-match melanoma PRS candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=melanoma and melanoma/cutaneous melanoma phenotyping). PGS000813 is best supported on visible evidence because it has strong endpoint alignment (familial cutaneous melanoma in non-carriers of CDKN2A mutation; still melanoma diagnosis), reports the strongest discrimination among listed direct melanoma models (full_model AUROC=0.77 with OR per SD=2.12), and has a coherent disease-focused multi-cohort development/validation context (multiple melanoma cohorts; EUR eval). Key limitation: its endpoint is a restricted familial/non-CDKN2A subgroup rather than a general-population melanoma endpoint, so generalizability is uncertain; additionally, most candidates report only full-model AUROC (not PGS-only), limiting strict PRS-only comparability. Runners-up were ranked by remaining direct-match support emphasizing endpoint fidelity plus reported discrimination/effect size: PGS000743 (general melanoma; AUROC=0.74 but small validation n=1,035 and heavy traditional risk-factor covariates), then PGS002247 and PGS002246 (incident invasive melanoma; AUROC~0.69 with R2 reported; clean age/sex covariates but smaller n=4,765), then PGS000766 (incident cutaneous melanoma; C-index=0.643 with HR=1.46; disease-focused multi-cohort but weaker reported discrimination).

All 6 listed candidates are direct lexical/EFO matches to multiple myeloma except PGS003450, which has an explicit endpoint mismatch (phenotyping_reported = Chronic lymphocytic leukemia) despite trait_reported saying Multiple myeloma, so it is deprioritized as endpoint-incoherent. Among the remaining coherent direct matches, PGS002281 has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported = Multiple myeloma), European evaluation ancestry, and the best-supported discrimination evidence in a reasonably sized validation (full-model AUROC 0.644 with CI 0.622–0.666; OR highest vs lowest quintiles 3.18). PGS002306 reports a higher full-model AUROC (0.69) but is limited by much smaller validation size (n=290) and unknown covariates, making its apparent advantage less reliable/comparable. The PRSweb scores (PGS000653/PGS000654/PGS000652) are endpoint-aligned and have explicit covariates (age/sex/PCs/batch) but show materially lower full-model AUROC (~0.576–0.577) and modest effect sizes; within that family, PGS000653 slightly edges PGS000654 on AUROC/R2. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because none of the candidates provide clearly PRS-only (covariate-free) performance metrics, and the top candidates’ reported AUROCs are full-model and thus not strictly comparable across differing/unknown covariate sets.

All 7 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (multiple sclerosis) by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, so a direct-match selection is possible. PGS002726 is preferred because it is disease-focused (IMSGC training cohort) and reports strong discrimination evidence for MS susceptibility (full-model AUROC 0.80 with an additional large effect-size signal: OR 15.0 for top 10% vs median), whereas several other candidates are from known UKB framework/portability papers (PGS001270/PGS001271 from the “813 traits” sparse framework; PGS001831/PGS002038 from the “Portability of 245 polygenic scores” framework) which domain guidance flags as systematically underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation. Main limitation: the key AUROC for PGS002726 is a full-model metric with covariates listed as Unknown and a small validation sample (n=938), and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; this keeps confidence at Moderate and the overall outcome at DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS000809 (disease-focused MS study context with reported full-model AUROC 0.765 and R² 0.069 under basic covariates), then the two portability-framework siblings with partial-r evidence (PGS002038 partial-r 0.0396 > PGS001831 partial-r 0.0367), then PGS004699 (MS-focused clinical-prediction context but not a pure MS-population endpoint—optic neuritis presentation—and only full-model AUROC reported).

Direct-match candidates for myocardial infarction are present (multiple models with trait_efo/phenotyping_reported explicitly myocardial infarction or acute myocardial infarction). The best-supported direct match from the visible list is PGS005039 because it is endpoint-aligned (Myocardial infarction; PheCode 411.2), comes from a disease-focused MI comparison paper (not a pan-trait UKB framework), and has the strongest visible per-SD effect size among the MI PheCode cluster (OR=1.578, 95% CI 1.50–1.67) alongside a high reported C-index (0.7848) in the selected European validation record. Runners-up are other highly similar MI PheCode 411.2 models from the same publication with slightly weaker OR/C-index evidence: PGS005035 (OR=1.541; C-index=0.7834), PGS005045 (OR=1.554; C-index=0.7839), PGS005044 (OR=1.546; C-index=0.7836), and then PGS005038 (OR=1.53; C-index=0.7831). Outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY) because across the direct-match set, many candidates report only full-model discrimination (C-index) without clearly PRS-only AUROC/R2, and several near-tied MI PheCode models are effectively indistinguishable on the available metadata, limiting certainty despite strong endpoint alignment.

Both visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = Nasal Cavity Polyp; phenotyping_reported = ICD10 J33 Nasal polyp) with identical ancestry context (DEV/EVAL EUR 100%), training cohort (UKB), training sample size (n=174,489), validation sample size (n=56,192), and the same publication/date. Neither reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2, so ranking must rely mainly on the available effect size and structural signals. PGS004535 is preferred because it reports a stronger per-SD odds ratio (OR=1.600668 vs 1.3496 for PGS004465), which domain guidance treats as stronger evidence of PRS discriminative power when AUC/R2 are missing. The main limitation is that covariates are listed as Unknown and there are no PRS-only discrimination metrics, so confidence is reduced and the choice is based largely on a single effect-size field within an otherwise near-clone pair.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to nicotine dependence via trait_efo and report the same endpoint label/phenotyping_reported: Tobacco use disorder) from the same UKB portability publication with similar basic covariates and identical training/validation sample sizes, so endpoint fidelity and study context do not separate them strongly. PGS002037 is preferred because it shows stronger reported PRS-comparable performance in the selected European validation record (partial-r 0.0741, CI 0.0601–0.0881) versus PGS001830 (partial-r 0.0557, CI 0.0416–0.0697), and it uses an LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage approach with substantially more variants (847,691 vs 13,838), which is a supportive structural signal for polygenic traits. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because both candidates come from a portability/framework-style UKB paper and neither provides standard PRS-only AUROC/R2 or effect-size metrics in the visible fields, limiting comparability and strength of evidence despite the direct trait match.

Direct-match candidates are present for nodular goiter, primarily the three models explicitly targeting benign nodular goiter (PGS005261/PGS005262/PGS005263) and two targeting nontoxic multinodular goiter (PGS001814/PGS002022). PGS005262 is best supported because it has the closest phenotype alignment to the target label (“Benign nodular goiter” with matching trait_efo) and, among the benign nodular goiter siblings, it shows the strongest visible validation performance (highest reported full-model AUROC: 0.5933) while using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) with very large variant count (~1.09M), a structural positive signal versus P+T. Runners-up: PGS005263 is the closest sibling (same endpoint family, PRSCS, similar variant count) but with lower AUROC; PGS005261 matches the endpoint but uses P+T with far fewer variants and weaker effect size (OR 1.048); PGS001814 and PGS002022 are still direct matches via the multinodular/nontoxic goiter concept and have basic covariates, but they come from a UKB portability framework paper and only report weak partial correlations (0.0277 and 0.024), with no AUC/R2/effect-size evidence shown. Main limitation lowering confidence: for the 2026 benign nodular goiter models, only full-model AUROC is provided (no PRS-only AUC/R2), covariates are “Unknown,” and the publication is a medRxiv preprint; these factors make performance comparability and robustness harder to judge from the visible metadata alone.

All 10 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (obesity) via trait_efo and/or phenotyping_reported. The best-supported choice from the visible evidence is PGS005235 because its endpoint fidelity is strong (phenotyping_reported: obesity phecode 278.1 despite trait_reported being broader “Adiposity”), it uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto) with high variant count (709,828), and it reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR≈1.97), which domain guidance treats as strong discrimination evidence when AUC/R2 are absent. Runners-up: PGS004447 is also endpoint-faithful (ICD10 E66 obesity), uses LDpred2 with very high variant count (~1.06M) and has a moderate OR (~1.36) but lacks PRS-comparable metrics; PGS005154 and PGS005145 are endpoint-faithful obesity scores evaluated in East Asian cohorts with large variant counts and reported betas, but their non-EUR-only evaluation makes them less generally supported absent a specified deployment ancestry; PGS002033 (UKB portability framework) has a relatively stronger partial correlation (0.0789) than its sibling PGS001825 but is penalized by the framework/portability study archetype and lacks clearer PRS-only AUC/R2. Overall confidence is limited because most candidates lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 and several have unknown covariates or framework-study penalties, making the ranking reliant on endpoint fidelity + method/variant structure + effect-size snippets rather than directly comparable performance metrics.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) via trait_efo=osteoporosis and phenotype labels that are either Osteoporosis or the closely aligned ICD10 M81 osteoporosis without pathological fracture. The strongest visible direct-match support comes from the 2024 Commun Biol study family (PGS004565/PGS004560/PGS004495/PGS004490): they are endpoint-faithful (Osteoporosis or M81) and report per-SD effect sizes, with PGS004565 showing the largest reported OR (1.328222) among that family, providing the best available PRS-discrimination signal in this context where many models lack PRS-only AUROC/R2. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS004560 has a nearly identical endpoint and similarly strong OR (1.320825); PGS002768 is endpoint-faithful and reports a moderate OR (1.31) but lacks other performance metrics and has a mixed trait_efo string; PGS004495 is the same study family with a smaller OR (1.1979). PGS001273 is included as the best-supported framework-style alternative because it provides explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 (PGS-only AUROC 0.5685; PGS R2 0.00688) with basic covariates, but it is penalized by its pan-trait sparse-framework origin ("across 813 traits"), and its high full-model AUROC is not treated as PRS-only evidence. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because the top-ranked Commun Biol candidates have unknown covariates and limited comparable PRS-only metrics (mostly OR-only), while the candidates with explicit PRS-only metrics come from framework/portability studies that domain guidance warns often underperform disease-focused models, leaving residual uncertainty.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to trait_efo=otosclerosis). PGS002046 is preferred because its phenotype is a straightforward otosclerosis endpoint (phenotyping_reported: "Otosclerosis") and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with very large variant count (570,308), which domain guidance generally favors for polygenic traits over sparse selection—especially when comparing framework-style scores. Its reported PRS-comparable metric is partial correlation (partial-r=0.0182, EUR validation), which is at least an explicit PRS-only-style signal, whereas PGS001255’s headline AUROC includes a full-model AUROC (0.6532) and the model is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often less externally robust.

Limitations: evidence is still limited/heterogeneous—PGS002046 lacks AUROC/R² and reports only partial-r, while PGS001255 provides more detailed AUROC/R² but is time-to-event ("TTE otosclerosis") and framework-derived; these differences make performance comparability imperfect and keep confidence below High. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (ovarian neoplasm) via ovarian cancer / ovarian carcinoma endpoints, with several explicitly mapped to ovarian neoplasm (e.g., PGS000544–PGS000564). PGS000082 is best supported overall because it has strong endpoint fidelity for a broad target (phenotyping_reported: incident ovarian cancer), large-scale multi-cohort disease-focused development/validation context, and comparatively strong reported discrimination among broad ovarian cancer models (full-model AUROC ~0.656 with standard epidemiologic covariates). Key limitation: the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics with multiple covariates (not PRS-only), so cross-model comparability is imperfect and lowers confidence.

Runners-up: PGS000793 is closely related (a re-weighted version of PGS000082) with similar endpoint and slightly higher full-model AUROC (~0.66) but is derivative rather than a primary disease score. PGS003394 (epithelial ovarian cancer; C-index ~0.623) has broad validation across multiple ancestries in evaluation and a large disease-consortium context, but its phenotype is framed as “10-year ovarian cancer risks,” which is closer to risk-wrapper packaging than a pure diagnosis endpoint. PGS005086 (non-mucinous epithelial ovarian cancer; AUROC ~0.607; OR ~1.46) has strong effect-size evidence and large validation, but is narrower than the umbrella target. PGS002250 shows strong HR (~1.49) and reasonable AUROC (~0.624) but is explicitly in BRCA2 carriers (restricted population), making it less general for an ovarian neoplasm target. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 11 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (pancreatic carcinoma) via pancreatic cancer / exocrine pancreatic carcinoma, with one clinically dominant subtype model (pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma) also plausibly aligned. PGS000083 is best supported overall because it has strong endpoint fidelity (incident pancreatic cancer), large European evaluation (n=391,491), and supportive effect-size evidence (HR=1.49, 95% CI 1.36–1.62) alongside reported discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.745; C-index 0.742). Key limitation: the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics with multiple covariates (including family history and smoking/BMI), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the standalone PRS contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; this keeps confidence below High. Runners-up: PGS000794 is essentially the same 22-variant score family with similar full-model AUROC/HR but uses inverse weights (making it less straightforward as a primary pick despite similar evidence). PGS000663 and PGS000725 are same-endpoint pancreatic cancer models with cleaner/simpler covariate sets than PGS000083 but show lower full-model AUROC (0.67 and 0.639, respectively) and/or much smaller validation (PGS000663 n=956). PGS002264 (ductal adenocarcinoma) reports a high AUROC (0.83) but is bundled with explicit clinical risk/diabetes-onset covariates and has non-reported evaluation ancestry, making its discrimination less PRS-comparable despite strong subtype alignment.

All 11 candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (trait_efo=Parkinson disease), but several have endpoint shifts toward progression/complications (PGS000056 cognitive decline in PD; PGS000211 motor decline; PGS000777 PD dementia) or are embedded in heavier non-genetic risk packaging (e.g., PGS001774 includes multiple established risk factors and family history; PGS004924 includes environmental exposures and self-reported smell). Among the models whose phenotyping_reported is simply Parkinson’s disease, the Lancet Neurology GWAS meta-analysis siblings (PGS000902/PGS000903) form the strongest coherent disease-focused cluster with large-scale development and basic covariates (PCs, age, sex). Between them, PGS000903 is preferred because it provides the strongest directly comparable discrimination evidence in the visible metadata (AUROC 0.692 plus R²=0.054 and OR top vs bottom quartile 6.25), whereas PGS000902 reports only a lower full-model AUROC (0.651) without PRS-comparable R²/OR. Confidence is not High because the reported AUROC values appear to be full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), covariate sets differ across candidates, and some other direct PD models show high full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS001774 AUROC 0.8) but are discounted due to heavier covariate packaging that makes metrics less comparable to standalone PRS performance.

All 4 candidates are direct matches by concept alignment to the target (peripheral vascular disease) via either the exact EFO term (PGS001843, PGS002055: peripheral vascular disease, unspecified) or the closely aligned clinical entity peripheral artery/arterial disease (PGS005158, PGS005217). PGS005217 is best supported overall because it is disease-focused for PAD with an incident endpoint (phenotyping_reported: incident peripheral artery disease), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (1,296,292), has broad multi-cohort development and multi-ancestry evaluation, and reports a strong PRS effect size (HR per SD 1.66). Main limitation: it is PAD (arterial) rather than the broader/unspecified PVD label, and the only discrimination metric shown is a full-model C-index (0.731) rather than a clearly PRS-only AUC/R2, so comparability to standalone PRS performance is uncertain.
